chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

Whoever performs Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwa for fifteen circuits, eight are dropped and he is counted with seven; and if he began with Al-Marwa, let him drop (it all) and let him begin with As-Safa.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa, one of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, the second hill in the Sa'i ritual
key_terms.طَرَحَ: Dropped or discarded (in the context of counting validity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one performs fifteen circuits of Sa'i or begins with the wrong pillar?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanics of Sa'i, affirming that fifteen circuits are valid with eight discarded to count as seven, while mandating a restart if one erroneously begins with Al-Marwa. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise order of rituals, linking the physical act to the spiritual commemoration of Hajar's search for water. The ruling underscores the importance of intentionality and correct sequence in fulfilling the pillar of Hajj.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘The one who performs Tawaaf between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa by fifteen circuits, eight would be dropped and he would be counted with seven; and if he began with Al-Marwa, so let him drop (it all) and let him begin with Al-Safa’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one performs fifteen times instead of seven times walking between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah he drops eight Shawt (walking once between al-Safa’ and al- Marwah) and counts the seven. If he begins from al-Marwah he must drop it and begin from al- Safa’.’”
